newsitem.title: USA: MIM to cut zinc concs to Europe - sources.
newsitem.headline: MIM to cut zinc concs to Europe - sources.

text.p: MIM Holdings Ltd has informed several European zinc smelters that it will cut by half the amount of zinc concentrates it will supply to them this year, European smelter sources said here on Sunday.

MIM said late last year it would cut production of zinc concentrates, but officials at European smelters said they were annoyed that the Australian company gave no notice period for the reduction in supplies, which will become effective with 1997 deliveries.
"It's unacceptable," a concentrates buyer at a European smelter told Reuters.
Among those said to have received the letter from MIM were Union Miniere SA, Outokumpu Oy and Billiton, a unit of Gencor Ltd.
It was unclear if MIM's shipments to Asia would be affected.
MIM officials were not immediately available at the conference for comment.

The European smelter sources also expressed irritation at the timing of the letter, which was received just before the world's zinc industry gathered here for the annual American Zinc Association conference.
The conference is seen as a key event in this year's "mating season" between zinc miners and smelters to determine treatment charges that the mines will pay the smelters.
The talks on treatment charges have already been dragged out by cuts in mine output, most notably at Anvil Range Mining Corp's Faro mine in Canada late last year.
Mining executives have said the cutbacks point to tighter concentrate supplies and thus justify lower treatment charges for smelters.

Mining officials said MIM's move would inevitably strengthen its hand further in talks with the smelters, while conference sources said it could bring additional delays in an agreement in the sensitive mine-smelter talks.

Industry and market sources at the conference said the treatment charge talks between the Australian mining companies and the Japanese smelters were closer to settlement than parallel negotiations involving European smelters.

The Asian talks have narrowed the gap to $10 a tonne, with mine firms seeking $165 and smelters seeking $175, based on an LME cash price of $1,000, but haggling continues over escalators, which allow smelters to reap the benefits of any rise in zinc prices. Many industry officials hold a bullish outlook on zinc.

With MIM's move seen putting a spoke in the wheel of the treatment charge talks, sentiment at the outset of the AZA conference was that there will be no benchmark set at the gathering this week. Treatment charges are usually set before or during the conference.

Some analysts also believed that the shutdown at Faro, combined with the development at MIM, would trigger a scramble for zinc concentrates that might lead to production cutbacks at European smelters.
One prominent analyst, who asked not to be named, said a great part of Faro's output went to Asturiana de Zinc SA and that the Spanish smelter could well have to cut output.
MIM is currently in negotiations with Asian smelters as well as European smelters.
-- Huw Jones, New York Commodity Desk +1-212-859-1646
